A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SeedPrints and retain identifiable corresponding methods and experiments. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original initialization-bias, training-lineage, distribution-shift and fingerprinting benchmark experiments, including additional Qwen results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds OLMo pretraining evaluations, null-distribution validation, hyperparameter ablations and cross-size analyses.

M1.justification: v1 uses simulated Gaussian reference correlations with t-tests or Mann–Whitney U-tests. v2 introduces an analytical Gaussian z-test on mean Kendall correlation and adopts it for the main results. Its simulated-null procedure also now includes identity-dimension selection and intersection. These change inference, while the underlying mean-based fingerprint extraction remains.

E1.justification: The principal coverage addition is OLMo-2-7B's heterogeneous-corpus pretraining trajectory, extending the existing controlled-pretraining scenario. The lineage-identification task, OpenWebText/TinyStories/The Stack experiments and six deployment transformations remain. Additional model sizes and catalog entries primarily expand experimental configurations.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain Intrinsic, REEF, PCS and ICS, with Gradient additionally evaluated on LeaFBench. The new experiments reuse these methods. HuRef in v2's cross-size comparison is already identified with PCS/ICS in v1, rather than establishing a new comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds comparisons of OLMo checkpoints against the final checkpoint, controlled sweeps of input count, sequence length and fingerprint size with accuracy/FPR metrics, and targeted cross-size Qwen comparisons. The reported LeaFBench pool expands from 58 to 65 models, and fine-tuning evaluation extends to Llemma at 700B tokens. These substantially expand evaluation protocols and configurations.

E4.justification: New analyses test the null approximation against approximately 2,500 independent-model pairs and Gaussian simulations (Appendix B), sensitivity to three hyperparameters (Table 8), and whether fingerprints collapse across model sizes within Qwen (Appendix D.3). The original continual-training and checkpoint analyses remain, largely relocated into Appendix D.

E5.justification: v2 adds analytical variance-based z-scores and one-sided Gaussian p-values, together with empirical assessment of the null approximation and dependence assumptions. The original ten-trial averaging remains documented for simulation-based results in Appendix D.2; an increase in repeated-run counts is not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial trajectory, ablation, null-validation, cross-size and pairwise results. Main-table p-values now use the analytical test, so their smaller magnitudes are not comparable performance gains. Table 7 reports Merge AUC 0.959 versus 1.000 under the revised detector/pool. Retained empirical-null results also change: Qwen s2000 versus s42 hidden-state t/U p-values change from 0.130/0.095 to 0.230/0.295 (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 9b).

T1.justification: v1 contains algorithmic definitions but no comparable theoretical development. v2 adds analytical-null derivations, formal noise and margin assumptions, stability and instability lemmas, and proofs of bottom-m recovery and sample-complexity bounds in Appendices B–C.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that initialization creates seed-specific fingerprints, these persist through training and distribution shifts, and SeedPrints supports birth-to-lifecycle attribution with strong deployment performance. The emphasis on large-scale pretraining and new empirical examples supports these existing claims rather than introducing a different core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a representation-contraction explanation for initialization bias and interpretations of hyperparameter sensitivity and null approximation. It explicitly discusses restricted-API limitations and qualifies merger robustness: interpolation with unrelated weights can dilute the fingerprint, explaining the reported merge failure. These are substantive additions to applicability and mechanism discussions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, states that both null implementations are provided, and documents softmax temperature 10 and detector defaults n=2000, length=1024 and m=0.1dout for Sections 5.2–5.3, plus separate ablation defaults. These materially improve implementation guidance; their disclosure alone does not establish changes to previously unspecified settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations connecting initialization bias to representation contraction (Li et al., 2026), Gaussian approximations to earlier work (Carlini et al., 2022; Lee et al., 2019), and the new OLMo/Llemma evaluations. The active/passive fingerprinting taxonomy and principal contrast with post-hoc methods remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, bias explanation and algorithm section are extensively rewritten. Contributions become an explicit list, lifecycle evaluation receives a separate subsection, and the appendices are reorganized with a contents page. Much existing experimental material moves into a consolidated simulation-based-results appendix.

P2.justification: v2 adds the OLMo trajectory and null-validation figures, substantially redraws the initialization-bias figure, and simplifies main experimental tables around analytical p-values. Earlier checkpoint plots are combined into Figure 5, while new ablation, cross-size and pairwise-results tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1's all-stage claim relied on controlled pretraining experiments with little null-model or hyperparameter validation. v2 adds a realistic OLMo trajectory, independent-model/null checks, ablations, implementation defaults and explicit deployment limitations, substantially strengthening empirical support and reproducibility. Gains are tempered by new inconsistencies: Lemma C.2 uses stronger noise assumptions than stated, and Table 5 incorrectly flags Intrinsic's 0.9470 Llemma score despite the stated 0.8 threshold.
